meta.title: Lattis, the free spreadsheet with the rigor of a database
meta.desc: Lattis is a free, local-first desktop spreadsheet: the flexibility of Excel, the rigor of a SQLite database, SQL, Lua scripts and connections to your databases.
hero.badge: Public beta available · Free for everyone
hero.sub: Lattis is a fast, modern desktop spreadsheet. You type just like in Excel, and it stores your data in real SQLite tables, on your own computer. And it stays free, for everyone.
hero.alt: Screenshot of Lattis: several tables on a single sheet
how.title: A spreadsheet that understands your data
how.sub: No schema to draw, no wizard to follow. Lattis watches what you type and does the database work for you.
how.s1d: Enter your data anywhere on the canvas, like in any spreadsheet. Nothing gets in the way of your typing.
how.s2d: It spots the block of data, highlights the header, infers each column's type and creates the matching SQLite table.
how.s3d: Your tables are real tables: SQL, formulas, pivot tables and charts run directly on the engine.
video.title: See Lattis in action
video.sub: Short videos covering the essentials. They are coming with the first public releases.
feat.title: Everything you need to analyze
feat.sub: Excel's most used features, powered by SQLite.
feat.1d: Several independent tables per sheet, each framed by a thin border. If one starts in A1, the sheet tab takes its name.
feat.2d: Text, integer, decimal, date, boolean. The type is detected as you type, never blocks your input, and can always be changed.
feat.3d: Everything fits in a single .lattis file, easy to send or archive, with crash recovery built in.
feat.4d: An Excel-like language with structured references such as Customers[City]. VLOOKUP becomes REFERENCE.
feat.5d: Query and edit your tables in SQL, with every object in the workbook listed right beside you.
feat.6d: Automate with db.query() and events. A safeguard stops infinite loops, so the interface never freezes.
feat.7d: Instant aggregations thanks to the engine's native GROUP BY, displayed as a tree.
feat.8d: Charts fed by your data, and Document tabs to lay out your analyses.
feat.9t: AI assistant, if you want it
feat.9d: An Assistant tab that is off by default, which you can connect to your own key or account.
show.1a: The Lattis SQL tab showing a result as a grid
show.1t: SQL and grid, side by side
show.1d: Run a GROUP BY in the SQL tab and the result appears as a grid you can sort, filter and reuse.
show.2a: Pivot table and chart in Lattis
show.2d: Pivot tables and charts rely on SQLite's native aggregation. They update as soon as your data changes.
show.3d: A simple, safe API to work on your tables in the background, with a built-in reference and warnings as you type.
conn.title: Connected to your databases
conn.sub: Import and refresh external data, Power Query style. Passwords stay in your computer's keychain.
conn.1d: PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite.
conn.2d: JSON REST APIs, Parquet and JSON files.
conn.3d: A “Lattis Server” on PostgreSQL, with roles and permissions. This feature is being designed and is not available yet.
price.title: Free. For everyone.
price.sub: No Pro edition, no subscription, no row limit. Lattis is free for individuals and companies alike, and it will stay that way.
price.i4: Your data stays on your machine
fund.title: So who funds Lattis?
fund.sub: The software is free for everyone because those who get the most value from it contribute in other ways.
fund.1d: Companies that rely on Lattis every day can support its development with a donation.
fund.2d: Partners fund specific features or back the roadmap, in full transparency.
fund.3d: Courses to get started with Lattis, SQL or Lua automation, for teams or individuals.
fund.4d: Help with rollout, migration from Excel, connecting your databases and custom scripts.
fund.cta: Support Lattis or get in touch
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: Yes. Every feature is free, for personal and professional use, with no subscription and no Pro edition. The project is funded by company donations, partnerships, training and business support.
faq.a2: On your computer. A workbook is a .lattis file containing a SQLite database. Nothing goes to a server unless you connect an external database yourself.
faq.q3: Will my Excel habits still work?
faq.a3: Yes: ribbon, context menus, shortcuts, undo and redo, familiar formulas. VLOOKUP is even converted to REFERENCE automatically.
faq.q4: Which systems does Lattis run on?
faq.a4: Windows, macOS and Linux. It is a native application built in Go with Wails and SvelteKit, without the weight of Electron.
faq.a5: Right now: a first beta is available for Windows, macOS and Linux. The Download button automatically fetches the latest version for your system.
faq.a6: Gladly: through a donation, a partnership, training for your teams or tailored support. Write to us at contact@lattis.be.

cta.sub: Try the beta and tell us what you think on GitHub.
